props.gloss_en: Rav: the mishnah's 'until they benefit' is not literal benefit, but any flame such that, were he standing near, he could use its light -- even at a distance
over dimming coals one does not bless
Rav Chisda: glowing coals are any such that, if one inserts a wood chip among them, it ignites by itself
Rav Chisda bar Avdimi said [the verse]: 'the cedars in the garden of God could not dim it' (Ezek 31:8)
the baraita's word is עוממות, with an ayin, as in the verse's עממהו (the resolution the תא שמע draws; the Hebrew gives only the verse, Steinsaltz states the reading)
Rava: 'until they benefit' means actual benefit from the light
Ulla: [the benefit is light] enough to tell an issar from a pundeyon
Chizkiya: enough to tell a Tiberian meluzma from a Tzippori meluzma
Rav Yehuda would bless over [the light of] the house of Adda the servant
Rava would bless over [the light of] the house of Gurya bar Chama
Abaye would bless over [the light of] the house of bar Avuh
Rav: one does not seek out fire the way one seeks out mitzvot
R' Zeira: at first I would seek out [fire]
R' Zeira: since I heard this of Rav Yehuda in Rav's name, I too do not seek it out
R' Zeira: but if it happens to come to me of itself, I bless
Rav Zevid: the dispute [of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel over one who ate and did not bless] is where he forgot
Rav Zevid: but where he did it deliberately, all agree he returns to his place and blesses
